sections.content: How many people are "CAD, drawing and architectural technicians"?

57,425 people

were counted on the census as "CAD, drawing and architectural technicians" in England and Wales in March 2021.
CAD, drawing and architectural technicians design and prepare technical drawings, plans, maps, charts and similar items and install, operate and maintain 3D printers.

People who had this job were generally similar in age to the working population

The occupation of "CAD, drawing and architectural technicians" had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 25 to 29 years. Of the whole working population 11.1% were aged 25 to 29 years. For people working as "CAD, drawing and architectural technicians", 16.2% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "CAD, drawing and architectural technicians" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "CAD, drawing and architectural technicians" included:

  • civil engineers
  • social and humanities scientists
  • photographers, audio-visual and broadcasting equipment operators

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "CAD, drawing and architectural technicians" there were more men than women (73.6% compared with 26.4%).

This means "CAD, drawing and architectural technicians" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "science, engineering and technology associate professionals".

Men made up 73.6% and women made up 26.4% of "CAD, drawing and architectural technicians"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "CAD, drawing and architectural technicians" included:

  • managers and proprietors in forestry, fishing and related services
  • physical scientists
  • senior police officers

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "CAD, drawing and architectural technicians" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged 50 years and older, we see there is a higher proportion of men with this occupation than women.

The percentage of men and women who are "CAD, drawing and architectural technicians" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "CAD, drawing and architectural technicians", 6.8% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (85.5% compared with 14.5%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (79.8%) than self-employed (20.2%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was London. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Hackney, this is in the same region of London.
